items.prompt: Which pair of conditions must hold for a rigid body to be in static equilibrium in a plane?

options.label: Sum of forces = 0 and sum of velocities = 0
Sum of forces = 0 and sum of moments = 0
Sum of forces = 0 and sum of masses = 0
Sum of moments = 0 and sum of energies = 0

rubric: Equilibrium requires zero net force and zero net moment.
Distractors substitute unrelated quantities such as velocity, energy or mass.

items.prompt: What is the SI unit of the moment of a force about a point?

options.label: N·s
N·m
N/m
N/m^2

rubric: Moment = force × perpendicular distance, giving N·m.
Distractors are units of stiffness, impulse and pressure.

items.prompt: What is a free-body diagram?

options.label: A graph of force plotted against displacement for a body
A scale drawing of a body showing its dimensions and materials
A sketch of an isolated body showing all external forces on it
A sketch of a whole structure showing only the internal forces between parts

rubric: An FBD isolates the body and shows all external loads and reactions.
Distractors confuse it with internal-force-only sketches, graphs or dimensioned drawings.

items.prompt: How many reaction components does a pin support exert on a body in a 2D problem?
rubric: A pin gives two force components (horizontal and vertical) and no moment.
3 is for a fixed support; 1 is for a roller.

items.prompt: What is a two-force member?

options.label: A member whose two ends are both fixed against rotation by supports
A member held in place by exactly two pin supports at its ends
A member loaded at only two points, with no couples
A member carrying two equal weights spaced along its length

rubric: Two-force members carry force along the line joining the two load points.
Distractors confuse it with supports, weights or fixed ends.

items.prompt: Which of the following are vector quantities? Select all that apply.

options.label: Force
Length of a beam
Mass of a block
Moment about a point

rubric: Force and moment have magnitude and direction.
Length and mass are scalars.

items.prompt: A student draws a free-body diagram of a ladder leaning on a smooth wall with its foot on rough ground. She needs to name the force from the smooth wall on the ladder. Which description is correct?

options.label: A force directed along the ladder, with friction along the wall
A normal force plus a friction force acting along the wall
A normal force perpendicular to the wall, no friction
A vertical force from the wall equal to the ladder's weight

rubric: A smooth surface can push only perpendicular to itself.
Distractors add friction or assume a direction unrelated to the contact surface.

items.prompt: A 100 N force acts at the end of a 2 m wrench, perpendicular to the wrench. Why does moving the force 1 m closer to the bolt halve the moment about the bolt?

options.label: Moment equals force divided by distance, so halving the distance would double it instead
Moment equals force times distance squared, so it falls to a quarter of its value
Moment equals force times perpendicular distance, so halving it halves the moment
Moment depends only on the size of the force, so moving it changes nothing at all

rubric: M = F·d, which is linear in distance.
Distractors misstate the formula.

items.prompt: A truss member is found to have a negative force value when using the convention that tension is positive. What does this mean?

options.label: The member carries no load
The member is in compression
The member has been drawn in the wrong place
The member is in tension

rubric: Negative under a tension-positive convention indicates compression.
Distractors misread sign as tension, zero load or a drawing error.

items.prompt: A block rests on a rough horizontal floor and is pushed with a small horizontal force that does not move it. What is the friction force?

options.label: Equal to the weight of the block
Zero, because the block is not moving
Equal to the push, in the opposite direction
Equal to the coefficient of static friction times the normal force

rubric: In equilibrium static friction balances the applied force and is below its limit.
The second option is only the maximum friction, reached at impending slip.

items.prompt: Why does a roller support provide only one reaction component?

options.label: It can resist motion only along the surface it rolls on, not across it
It resists only vertical motion regardless of the surface
It resists rotation but allows all translation
It resists motion only perpendicular to the surface it rolls on

rubric: A roller is free to move along its surface, so the reaction is normal to it.
Distractors reverse the direction or invent rotation resistance.

items.prompt: Where is the centroid of a uniform rectangle of width b and height h, measured from its bottom-left corner?

options.label: (b, h)

rubric: Symmetry puts the centroid at the middle.
The thirds apply to triangles, not rectangles.

items.prompt: A beam in static equilibrium is loaded by several forces. Which statements correctly describe the situation? Select all that apply.

options.label: The beam must have no support reactions
The sum of vertical forces is zero
The sum of moments is zero about any chosen point
Every individual force on the beam must be zero

rubric: Equilibrium means net force and net moment vanish about any point.
Individual forces need not vanish, and reactions are usually present.

items.prompt: A uniform 4 m beam weighing 200 N rests on a pin at its left end and a roller at its right end. No other loads act. A student predicts the vertical reaction at the roller. Which prediction is correct?

options.label: 200 N, because the roller carries the full weight of the beam
100 N, because the weight acts at midspan and is shared equally
0 N, because a roller cannot resist weight, only the pin can
50 N, because the roller is only one of the four metres of span

rubric: Symmetric support of a uniform beam splits the weight equally.
Distractors ignore the pin or misunderstand roller capability.

items.prompt: What does a free-body diagram of a rigid body show?

options.label: The body isolated from its surroundings, with every external force and moment on it
The body with each force drawn as components along the direction of greatest stress
The body with only the applied loads drawn, since support reactions are found later
The body joined to its supports, with the internal forces between its parts drawn in

rubric: A free-body diagram isolates the body and shows all external forces and moments, including support reactions.
Distractors wrongly include internal forces or omit reactions.

items.prompt: A constant force pushes perpendicular to a wrench handle. Which change doubles the moment about the bolt?

options.label: Applying the same force twice as far from the bolt
Halving the force and halving the distance to the bolt
Doubling the mass of the wrench handle
Pushing at the same point but along the handle

rubric: Moment = force x perpendicular distance, so doubling the distance doubles the moment.
Pushing along the handle gives zero moment, and halving both quarters it.

items.prompt: Why does a straight truss member pinned at both ends, with no load between the pins, carry only axial tension or compression?

options.label: Only two forces act on it, so equilibrium requires them to be equal, opposite and collinear
Truss members are rigid, so pin forces cannot cause them to deform in any way
Its weight is much larger than the pin forces, so it dominates the member's behavior
Pins cannot transmit moments, so every force on it must be perpendicular to its length

rubric: A two-force member in equilibrium has collinear equal and opposite forces along the line joining the pins.
Distractors misuse the pin-moment idea or rigidity.

items.prompt: A couple is two equal, opposite, parallel forces separated by a distance d. Which statement about its moment is correct?

options.label: It has the same value about every point, since the net force is zero
It equals one force times the distance from the point to the nearer force
It depends on the point chosen and is zero only at the midpoint between forces
It is zero, because the two forces cancel each other out

rubric: A couple's moment is F x d about any point because the force sum is zero.
Distractors confuse zero net force with zero moment or make it point dependent.

items.prompt: A crate rests on a rough floor and is pushed horizontally with a force too small to make it slide. How does the friction force compare with the push?

options.label: It equals the maximum value, μs times the normal force, because friction always acts at its limit
It is zero, because the crate is not moving relative to the floor
It is smaller than the push, because friction only resists part of the applied load
It equals the push in magnitude and is opposite, because the crate stays in equilibrium

rubric: Static friction adjusts to balance the push, up to its maximum.
Distractors assume friction is always at its limit or absent at rest.

items.prompt: Which of the following are conditions for a rigid body in a plane to be in static equilibrium? Select all that apply.

options.label: The sum of moments about any point is zero
Each individual force on the body produces zero moment
The sum of the force components in the y direction is zero
The sum of the magnitudes of all forces is zero
The sum of the force components in the x direction is zero

rubric: 2D equilibrium requires zero net force components and zero net moment.
Summing magnitudes or requiring each moment to vanish are incorrect.

items.prompt: A uniform rectangular steel plate has a circular hole cut out, with the hole centered to the left of the plate's geometric center. A technician wants to know how the hole changes the location of the centroid compared to the solid plate. Which statement is correct?

options.label: The centroid moves to the hole's center, because that point now defines the shape
The centroid stays at the geometric center, since the plate is still uniform
The centroid moves to the right, away from the hole, because less area remains on the left
The centroid moves to the left, toward the hole, because the hole removes material there and the plate is lighter on that side

rubric: Removing area on the left shifts the centroid right, away from the hole.
Distractors ignore the removed area or move the centroid the wrong way.

items.prompt: A 100 N force acts at the end of a 2 m bar, at 30 degrees to the bar's axis. What is the moment about the other end of the bar?

options.label: 87 N·m

rubric: 173 and 87 come from using cosine or mixing angle components.

items.prompt: A simply supported beam is 6 m long with a pin at A (left) and a roller at B (right). A 12 kN vertical load acts 2 m from A. What is the vertical reaction at B?

options.label: 8 kN
12 kN
6 kN
4 kN

rubric: Moments about A: By x 6 = 12 x 2, so By = 4 kN.
8 kN is the reaction at A, and the others ignore moment balance.

items.prompt: A distributed load rises linearly from 0 to 6 kN/m over a 3 m length. What is the equivalent single force and where does it act?

options.label: 9 kN, 2 m from the zero end
18 kN, 2 m from the zero end
18 kN, 1.5 m from the zero end
9 kN, 1.5 m from the zero end

rubric: Triangle area = 0.5 x 3 x 6 = 9 kN, acting at two-thirds of the length from the zero end, i.e. 2 m.
Others forget the half factor or place it at the midpoint.

items.prompt: A 500 N crate rests on a floor with μs = 0.4. A horizontal push of 150 N is applied and the crate does not move. What is the friction force on the crate?
rubric: The crate is in equilibrium, so friction equals the push, 150 N, which is below the 200 N limit.
200 N assumes friction is at its maximum.

items.prompt: At the apex joint of a symmetric truss, a 10 kN load acts downward. Two members meet there, each at 30 degrees to the horizontal and sloping down to the supports. What is the force in each member?

options.label: 10 kN compression
20 kN compression
10 kN tension
5 kN compression

rubric: Vertical balance: 2F sin30 = 10 gives F = 10 kN, and the members push on the joint, so compression.
5 kN omits the second member, and 20 kN uses the wrong trig function.

items.prompt: A beam is pinned at A and rests on a roller at B on a horizontal surface. A vertical load acts on it. Which reactions appear on its free-body diagram? Select all that apply.

options.label: Vertical reaction at A
Horizontal reaction at A
A reaction couple at B
Vertical reaction at B
Horizontal reaction at B

rubric: A pin gives two force components and a roller gives one force perpendicular to the surface.
A horizontal force or couple at the roller is not possible.

items.prompt: An L-shaped plate is made of a 6 m wide by 2 m tall rectangle along the bottom, plus a 2 m wide by 4 m tall rectangle standing on top of it at one end. The base is at y = 0. Using composite areas, what is the height of the centroid above the base?
rubric: Areas are 12 and 8 with centroids at y = 1 and y = 4, so ybar = (12 + 32)/20 = 2.2 m.
Other values come from averaging heights or ignoring area weights.

items.prompt: A simply supported beam of length 6 m has supports at A (left end) and B (right end). A 12 kN point load acts downward 2 m from A. The beam's weight is negligible. What is the vertical reaction at B?

options.label: 6 kN
8 kN
2 kN
4 kN

rubric: Moments about A give B(6) = 12(2), so B = 4 kN.
8 kN comes from using the distance from B instead of from A.

items.prompt: At an unloaded pin joint of a truss, three members meet and two of them are collinear. What is the force in the third member?

options.label: Half the collinear force, because it shares the load with the other two members.
Equal to the force in the collinear members, because the joint must be symmetric.
Zero, because its perpendicular component is the only one with nothing to balance it.
Undetermined, because three unknowns exceed the two joint equations available.

rubric: Only the third member has a component perpendicular to the collinear pair, and nothing balances it, so it is a zero-force member.
The 'undetermined' distractor ignores that the collinear members can balance each other.

items.prompt: A block rests on a rough incline. What is the minimum coefficient of static friction needed for the block to stay at rest on a 30 degree incline?
rubric: At impending slip mu = tan(30) = 0.58.
0.50 (sin) and 0.87 (cos) come from using one component rather than the ratio of the two.

items.prompt: An L-shaped plate is made of two rectangles. Rectangle 1 spans x = 0 to 6 and y = 0 to 2. Rectangle 2 spans x = 0 to 2 and y = 2 to 6. What is the x-coordinate of the plate's centroid?
rubric: Areas are 12 and 8 with centroid x of 3 and 1, so x = (36+8)/20 = 2.2.
3.0 ignores the second rectangle and 2.0 comes from averaging the centroid positions without area weights.

items.prompt: A 200 N force acts at 30 degrees above the horizontal at the end of a horizontal wrench handle 0.5 m long, measured from the bolt axis. What is the magnitude of the moment about the bolt?

options.label: 50 N·m
25 N·m

rubric: Only the perpendicular component counts: 200 sin30 x 0.5 = 50 N·m.
86.6 N·m uses the cosine component, which is parallel to the handle and gives no moment.

items.prompt: A planar rigid body in equilibrium has three unknown reaction components. Which sets of three equilibrium equations are independent and sufficient to solve for them? Select all that apply.

options.label: ΣM about A, ΣM about B and ΣM about C, with A, B, C not collinear
ΣM about A, ΣM about B and ΣFx, with line AB parallel to the y-axis
ΣM about A, ΣM about B and ΣM about C, with A, B, C on one line
ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, ΣM about point A = 0

rubric: Two force equations plus one moment, or three moments about non-collinear points, are independent.
Moments about collinear points, or two moments with a force sum perpendicular to line AB, leave a resultant along AB unconstrained.

items.prompt: A 3 m horizontal beam of negligible weight is pinned to a wall at A. A cable runs from the free end B up to the wall, making 30 degrees with the horizontal beam. A 400 N sign hangs from B. What is the cable tension?
rubric: Moments about A: T sin30 x 3 = 400 x 3, so T = 800 N.
462 N (400/cos30) and 693 N (400/tan30) use the wrong trigonometric component for the perpendicular force.

items.prompt: A student cuts a section through four members of a determinate planar truss. No three of the cut members are concurrent or parallel, and no member force is known. Why can't this one section give any single member force by itself?

options.label: Section cuts only work after the support reactions on the kept portion have been set to zero first.
The kept portion gives only three independent equilibrium equations, fewer than the four unknown forces.
Sections only work when the cut crosses exactly two members, because each moment equation needs two lines of action.
A cut through more than three members always means the truss is statically indeterminate as a whole structure.

rubric: A planar free body gives three equations, so four unknown member forces cannot be solved from one cut.
Distractors claim a rule on member count that is not a real restriction; determinate trusses can still have cuts through four members.

items.prompt: A frame has bodies AB and BC joined by a frictionless pin at B. A student draws separate free-body diagrams and shows the pin force on AB as 5 kN to the right and on BC as 5 kN to the right. What is the error?

options.label: A frictionless pin transmits only a couple, so the forces at B should be drawn as moments.
The pin forces on the two bodies must be equal and opposite by Newton's third law, so one arrow points left.
The pin force must be split into components, because a pin cannot transmit a single resultant force.
The pin forces should have different magnitudes, because the bodies have different weights and reactions at B.

rubric: Interaction forces at an internal joint are equal and opposite on the two bodies.
The other options invent restrictions on pins that do not exist.

items.prompt: A block of weight W on a rough floor is pulled by a rope at angle theta above the horizontal with force P. A student says slip is impending when P cos(theta) = mu W. What is wrong with this analysis?

options.label: Friction at impending slip should be mu times P rather than mu times the normal force, so the student's friction term is too small.
The rope's vertical component adds to the floor's support, so N = W + P sin(theta) and slip needs a larger pull.
The normal force should be W reduced by the factor cos(theta), so the friction limit is lower than the student used.
The rope's vertical component partly lifts the block, so N = W - P sin(theta) and slip needs a smaller pull.

rubric: The vertical rope component reduces the normal force: P cos(theta) = mu(W - P sin(theta)).
Several distractors misplace the rope's vertical component or the friction law.

items.prompt: A uniform ladder rests against a smooth vertical wall with its foot on a rough floor, and it is at rest. Which statement correctly describes the floor's contact force on the ladder?

options.label: It is vertical, since a floor can only push perpendicular to its surface and wall contact is smooth.
It points along the ladder, since the ladder is a two-force member held by the wall and the floor.
It has a horizontal component toward the wall, since friction must balance the horizontal push of the wall.
It has a horizontal component pointing away from the wall, since friction opposes the ladder's tendency to lean on the wall.

rubric: The wall's push is horizontal and away from the wall, so floor friction must point toward the wall to give zero net horizontal force.
A vertical floor force would leave the wall's push unbalanced.

items.prompt: A single rigid planar beam carries general loads in its plane. Each support arrangement below is properly oriented so the beam is stable, and the support reactions are the only unknowns. Which arrangement makes the beam statically indeterminate?

options.label: A pin at one end and a link at the other, with the link line of action not passing through the pin
A pin at one end and a roller at the other, with the roller surface not parallel to the beam axis
Pins at both ends, with each pin free to transmit force in any in-plane direction
A fixed support at one end only, with the other end completely free of supports

rubric: Two pins give four reaction components against three equilibrium equations.
The other arrangements each give exactly three unknowns.

items.prompt: A uniform ladder leans against a smooth wall and rests on a rough floor, and it is close to slipping at the foot. Which changes would make slipping less likely? Select all that apply.

options.label: Fitting the feet with higher-friction rubber pads
Having the user climb higher before standing still
Moving the foot farther from the wall at the same ladder length
Setting the ladder at a steeper angle to the floor

rubric: The required friction coefficient falls as the ladder gets steeper, and higher available friction raises the limit.
Climbing higher or moving the foot out increases the horizontal wall force that friction must balance.

items.prompt: A boom AB is pinned to the ground at A and raised by a hydraulic cylinder CD pinned at C on the boom and at D on the ground. The cylinder's weight is negligible and it carries no load between its pins. A student models the cylinder force as perpendicular to the boom at C and gets a result far from the measured value. What is the flaw?

options.label: The cylinder force must be vertical, since the ground pin at D can only resist vertical load.
A cylinder loaded only at its two pins is a two-force member, so its force acts along line CD.
The cylinder force direction is undetermined, since a pinned member can push at any angle.
The cylinder force must act along the boom, since the boom carries all load axially to the pin at A.

rubric: With forces only at two pins and no couple, equilibrium requires the force to act along the line joining the pins.
The other options assign directions with no basis in the two-force member condition.

items.prompt: At joint D of a plane truss, members DA and DB are collinear and horizontal, and member DC rises at 40° above horizontal. A 5 kN external load acts horizontally at D. What is the force in DC?

options.label: 5 / cos 40° kN
5 tan 40° kN
Zero
5 sin 40° kN

rubric: Summing forces perpendicular to the collinear members gives F_DC sin 40° = 0, so DC carries nothing.
Distractors apply the load to DC as though the collinear members could not absorb a horizontal load.

items.prompt: A uniform ladder rests on a rough floor against a smooth vertical wall and is in equilibrium. Treating it as a three-force body, what is the direction of the floor reaction at the foot?

options.label: Tilted away from the wall, because the wall pushes the ladder outward and friction must balance it
Tilted toward the wall, through the point where wall force and weight lines cross
Vertical, because the smooth wall carries no load and the floor only supports the weight
Along the ladder, because the ladder acts as a two-force member between its contacts

rubric: Three non-parallel coplanar forces must be concurrent; the horizontal wall force and vertical weight meet above the foot, and friction toward the wall tilts the floor reaction that way.
Distractors ignore friction or treat a loaded ladder as a two-force member.

items.prompt: A beam AB of length L carries a triangular load rising from zero at A to w (N/m) at B. A student replaced it with a resultant of wL/2 acting at midspan and got wrong reactions. Which step is faulty?

options.label: The resultant should act at 2L/3 from A, the triangle's centroid, not at midspan
The resultant is right, but moments need the load kept distributed, not replaced
Magnitude should be wL/3, because the load varies linearly along the span
Magnitude should be wL, because the peak intensity acts along the full span

rubric: The area wL/2 is right, but the resultant acts through the centroid of the triangle, 2L/3 from the zero end.
Distractors misjudge the magnitude or wrongly claim a resultant cannot be used for moments.

items.prompt: A uniform crate of weight W, 0.4 m wide and 1.2 m tall, sits on a floor with μs = 0.5. A slowly increasing horizontal push P is applied 0.9 m above the floor. What happens first?

options.label: It slips first, at P = 0.5W, before the moment can reach tipping
It slips and tips together, since friction acts at the same instant
It tips first, at P ≈ 0.44W, using the full 0.4 m width as the arm
It tips first, at P ≈ 0.22W, well below the slip threshold of 0.5W

rubric: Tipping needs P(0.9) = W(0.2), so P ≈ 0.22W, which is below the slip load of 0.5W.
Distractors use the full width as the restoring arm or assume slipping always comes first.

items.prompt: A stable plane truss has 7 joints and 12 members, and its supports supply 3 reactions. How should it be classified for static analysis?

options.label: Indeterminate to the first degree
Unstable, with too few members
Statically determinate
Indeterminate to the second degree

rubric: Unknowns m + r = 15 exceed the 2j = 14 equations, so there is one redundant.
Distractors miscount the equations or confuse indeterminacy with instability.

items.prompt: A straight link has frictionless pins at both ends, negligible weight and no loads between the pins. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.label: The link can only be in tension, since nothing loads it between the pins
The two pin forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
The force at each pin acts along the line joining the pins
Each pin force has a perpendicular component that balances the link's bending

rubric: With two forces on a body in equilibrium, they must be collinear, equal and opposite.
Distractors invent a bending reaction or wrongly exclude compression.

items.prompt: A plane truss has horizontal top chord BC and horizontal bottom chord GF, joined by a diagonal BG. A section cut passes through BC, BG and GF, and you want the force in BC alone from a single equation on the cut portion. Which equation does that?

options.label: Sum of moments about G, where the lines of BG and GF meet
Sum of horizontal forces on the cut portion
Sum of vertical forces on the cut portion
Sum of moments about B, where the lines of BC and BG meet

rubric: Moments about G remove BG and GF, leaving only BC.
Moments about B isolate GF, vertical forces isolate BG, and horizontal forces involve all three.

items.prompt: You need the force in one mid-span member of a 15-joint truss with known reactions. Criteria: fewest equations and least error propagation. Which approach is best?

options.label: Mark members as zero-force unless a joint carries an external load
Method of sections: cut the target and two others, then solve
Method of joints at all 15 joints, solving the full set together
Method of joints from a support, advancing joint by joint until the target

rubric: A section through the target and at most two other members gives the force with one or two equations and no accumulated error.
Joint-by-joint approaches take many more equations and compound arithmetic errors.

items.prompt: A freestanding sign of weight W is overturned by a fixed wind force at a set height. Criterion: the largest increase in tipping margin (restoring moment ÷ overturning moment). Which change is best?

options.label: Add ballast raising the weight 30%, so the margin rises 30%
Lower the wind-load height by 20%, so the margin rises 25%
Fit a rubber pad with higher friction, so the base resists sliding more and the margin rises
Widen the base from 1.0 m to 1.4 m, so the margin rises 40%

rubric: Widening raises the restoring moment W·b/2 by 40%, more than ballast (30%) or lowering the load height (about 25% margin gain).
Friction affects slipping, not tipping.

items.prompt: A 50 N block rests on a floor with μs = 0.4. A student says a 10 N horizontal push produces 20 N of friction because F = μN. Which critique is best?

options.label: Friction is 10 N; μsN = 20 N is only the maximum, reached at impending slip
Friction is 0 N, since static friction acts only once the block begins to slide
Friction is 4 N, since μs multiplies the push rather than the normal force
Friction is 20 N, since the floor always supplies μsN and the block pushes back equally

rubric: For a block at rest, friction equals the applied push (10 N) and μsN is only the upper limit.
Distractors treat μN as always acting or misplace where μ applies.

items.prompt: A 12 m steel girder sees large temperature swings. Criteria: statically determinate, stable, and no thermal stress from expansion. Which end supports are best?

options.label: Rollers at both ends, so it can expand freely in either direction
A pin at each end, so horizontal reactions hold it firmly in place
A pin at one end and a roller at the other, so it expands freely
A fixed support at one end and a roller at the other, for rotational stiffness

rubric: Pin plus roller gives three reactions, a determinate stable system, and free expansion.
Two pins or a fixed end restrain expansion; two rollers leave horizontal motion unrestrained.

items.prompt: A student draws a free-body diagram of a whole two-member frame, including the equal and opposite pin forces between the members, then applies ΣF = 0. Which critique is best?

options.label: They should be kept but resolved into components, since only the vector sum of the pin forces is zero
Only one arrow should appear at the pin, because the other force acts on the other member and not on this body
Internal pin forces cancel in pairs, so omit them; only external loads and reactions belong
Correct, because each pin force must be drawn on the diagram for the whole body to be in equilibrium

rubric: On a whole-structure FBD, internal forces are equal and opposite and so never appear.
Distractors treat internal forces as external loads.

items.prompt: A beam's support reactions were found from ΣFx, ΣFy and moments about A. Which checks give independent confirmation of the result? Select all that apply.

options.label: Redo the moment equation about A with the same arithmetic
Confirm each support carries half the total load, as symmetry suggests
Take moments about a different point B using all loads and the computed reactions
Move the load to support A and confirm the reaction at the other support is zero

rubric: A moment sum about a new point and a limiting-case test both check the answer independently.
Half-load reactions hold only for symmetric loading, and repeating the same equation is not independent.

items.prompt: A horizontal boom is pinned to a wall and carries a 10 kN vertical load at its free end. A tie rod runs from that end to the wall at angle θ above horizontal. The tie is rated for 18 kN and the wall anchor can take at most 12 kN horizontal pull; ignore the boom's weight. Which θ meets both limits?
rubric: Moments about the pin give T = 10/sin θ and the horizontal pull is 10/tan θ; at 45° these are 14.1 kN and 10 kN, within both limits.
35° passes the tie rating (17.4 kN) but the horizontal pull is 14.3 kN; 25° and 30° exceed the tie rating.

items.prompt: A planar truss has 7 joints, 11 members and 3 support reaction components. A colleague says that 11 + 3 = 2 x 7, so it is determinate and stable and joint equations will give every member force. Which critique is soundest?

options.label: The count is invalid because support reactions must never be included when comparing member numbers to the joint equations.
The count shows redundancy, because m + r equal to 2j means one member more than the minimum for stability is present.
The count proves stability, but joint equations cannot be used because pinned joints transmit moments between members.
The count is only necessary; a braced region plus a mechanism elsewhere can still meet it, so stability needs a separate check.

rubric: m + r = 2j is necessary for determinacy but does not guarantee geometric stability; a mechanism in one part can be offset by redundancy in another.
Distractors treat the count as proof or misread what equality means.

items.prompt: A uniform rectangular crate, 0.2 m long along the slope and 0.6 m tall, rests on a rough incline with static friction coefficient 0.5. The incline is raised slowly. Which judgement about the first failure is correct?

options.label: It slides at about 18°, because friction is weakest when the centre of gravity sits high on the crate.
It tips at about 18°, because tan θ reaches width/height = 1/3 before it reaches the friction coefficient 0.5.
It tips at about 59°, because tipping needs tan θ to reach the height-to-width ratio of 3.
It slides at about 27°, because tan θ reaches the friction coefficient 0.5 before it reaches the ratio 1/3.

rubric: Tipping begins when tan θ = b/h = 1/3 (about 18°), which is lower than the sliding threshold tan θ = 0.5 (about 27°).
Distractors invert the ratio or assume sliding always comes first.

items.prompt: A simply supported beam carries a triangular load over its whole span. An analyst replaces it with its single resultant at the load's centroid, then uses that to get both the support reactions and the shear at mid-span. Judge this approach.

options.label: Both results are right, because statically equivalent loads give identical internal forces at every section of the beam.
Neither result is right, because a resultant can never represent a distributed load in any rigid-body analysis.
Reactions are right, but the mid-span shear needs only the load on one side of the cut, not the whole-span resultant.
Reactions are wrong, but shear is right, because the resultant must be placed at mid-span for any symmetric beam.

rubric: Equivalence holds for the external reactions of the whole body, but internal forces at a cut depend on how the load is distributed on each side of it.
Distractors extend equivalence to internal forces or reject it entirely.

items.prompt: In a frame, straight member BC is pinned at B and C and carries a 400 N vertical load at its midpoint. To save equations, a student treats BC as a two-force member with force directed along BC. Evaluate this assumption.

options.label: Invalid, because a load between the pins makes it a multiforce member, so each pin needs two unknown components.
Invalid, because a two-force member must be vertical, so a force directed along a tilted BC is not allowed.
Valid, because any straight member with pins at both ends is a two-force member whatever loads act along its length.
Invalid, because pins at both ends force the member to act as a beam fixed at B and C carrying end moments.

rubric: A two-force member has forces at only two points; the midspan load makes three, so the pin forces are not confined to the BC line.
Distractors keep the two-force label or invent moment or orientation requirements.

items.prompt: A rope wraps 1.5 turns round a fixed bollard and is just about to slip while holding a boat. An engineer proposes a bollard of twice the radius, with the same rope and wrap, to double the holding capacity. Evaluate the proposal.

options.label: Capacity halves, because a larger radius lowers the normal pressure on the rope and so lowers friction.
Capacity rises by about e^2, because the radius appears in the exponent alongside the friction coefficient.
Capacity doubles, because contact length doubles while the pressure per unit length on the rope stays the same.
No gain, because T2/T1 = e^(μβ) depends on friction and wrap angle, not on drum radius.

rubric: The capstan equation depends only on μ and the wrap angle β, so changing radius leaves the ratio unchanged.
Distractors assume radius changes contact friction in a way the equation does not include.

items.prompt: A large pin-jointed truss is loaded and you need only the force in one mid-span member. Which statements justify using the method of sections rather than the method of joints? Select all that apply.

options.label: Only the part of the truss on one side of the cut is analysed, so unrelated joints need not be solved.
Support reactions are not needed when the cut is made, since the isolated section is in equilibrium under the internal member forces alone.
A cut may pass through four or more members, because the three equilibrium equations can be applied again to each joint on the cut.
A cut through the member and at most two others lets moments about a well-chosen point give the force directly.

rubric: Sections avoid solving the whole truss and work when a cut exposes at most three unknowns that are not concurrent or parallel.
Distractors ignore the three-unknown limit or claim reactions are never required.

items.prompt: A 5 m uniform ladder weighing 200 N leans at 60° to the ground against a smooth wall; the floor has static friction coefficient 0.3. An 800 N worker climbs to the very top. Judge the setup against the criterion that required friction must not exceed available friction. Which assessment is correct?

options.label: It slips: required friction is about 1560 N, above the 300 N available at the floor.
It holds: required friction is about 58 N, below the 300 N available at the floor.
It holds: required friction is about 290 N, below the 300 N available at the floor.
It slips: required friction is about 520 N, above the 300 N available at the floor.

rubric: Moments about the foot give wall force = (100 + 800) cot 60° ≈ 520 N, which equals required friction; available is 0.3 x 1000 = 300 N.
Distractors use tan instead of cot, place the worker mid-ladder, or count only the ladder weight.

items.prompt: A square pin-jointed panel ABCD must resist a horizontal wind load that reverses direction. Bracing must be slender cables (tension only), using as few members as possible. Which design meets all constraints?

options.label: A horizontal cable joining the mid-points of the two vertical sides, so the panel cannot shear under load.
Two parallel cables along diagonal AC, one on each face, so that either cable resists a load reversal.
One cable along each diagonal, so whichever is in tension resists each direction of the load.
One cable along diagonal AC, since it resists the load in either direction by switching between tension and compression.

rubric: Cables carry tension only, so each load direction needs its own diagonal; two crossed diagonals are the minimum.
Distractors rely on cable compression, duplicate one diagonal, or add a member that does not stop shear.

items.prompt: A designer supports a planar platform with three two-force links, whose lines of action all pass through one point P, claiming three reactions restrain the three planar degrees of freedom. What is the design missing?

options.label: A requirement that the links be perpendicular to the platform, so that every reaction is a purely vertical force.
Moment reactions at the link ends, because two-force links cannot transmit any moment to the platform.
A fourth link, because three reactions are never enough to restrain a planar body, however the links lie.
Link lines that neither meet at one point nor are all parallel, so the links can resist moment about P.

rubric: Concurrent or parallel link lines give improper constraint: no link can resist moment about P, so the platform can rotate.
Distractors claim three links never suffice, demand moment reactions, or impose a false orientation.

items.prompt: A square-thread screw jack must self-lock under load (lead angle no larger than the friction angle) and lift as far as possible per turn. Thread friction coefficient is 0.15 (friction angle about 8.5°). Which lead angle should be specified?
rubric: Self-locking needs lead angle ≤ atan(0.15) ≈ 8.5°; the largest listed value that meets it gives the fastest lift, 8°.
12° and 16° would overhaul; 4° locks but lifts less per turn than necessary.

items.prompt: A tower crane needs a 40 kN counterweight at distance d on the side opposite the load. The 10 kN jib weight acts 5 m from the tower axis on the load side; the 20 kN hook load acts 12 m out. Constraints: loaded, net moment about the axis is at most 40 kN·m in magnitude; unloaded, the net moment toward the counterweight side is at most 250 kN·m. Which d meets both?
rubric: Loaded: |290 - 40d| ≤ 40 gives 6.25 ≤ d ≤ 8.25; unloaded: 40d - 50 ≤ 250 gives d ≤ 7.5. So d = 7.0 m works.
8.0 m fails the unloaded limit (270), while 5.5 m and 9.0 m fail the loaded limit.

items.prompt: A three-hinged arch has pins at both supports A and B and an internal hinge C at the crown, with several vertical and horizontal loads. Which solution plan yields all four support reaction components using only equilibrium?

options.label: Write moment equations about A and B for the whole arch plus one force sum, since the hinge at C adds no further equation.
Write the three overall equilibrium equations only, because the four unknowns reduce to three once the hinge is ignored.
Treat each half as a two-force member, so each support reaction acts along the line from its support to hinge C.
Take the three overall equations, then a moment equation about C for one half, since the hinge carries no moment.

rubric: Four unknowns need a fourth independent equation; zero moment at the hinge for one half provides it.
Distractors use only the three whole-body equations or wrongly call the loaded halves two-force members.

items.prompt: A planar pin-jointed truss has j joints and m = 2j - 3 members, and is stable and determinate on a pin and a roller. You must extend it. Which extensions keep it determinate and stable? Select all that apply.

options.label: Add one new joint connected to two existing joints by two non-collinear members.
Add two new joints, each joined to two existing joints by two non-collinear members.
Add one new joint connected to three existing joints by three members.
Add one new joint connected to two existing joints by two collinear members.

rubric: Each new joint with two non-collinear members adds 2 members per joint, preserving m = 2j - 3 and stability.
Collinear members create a mechanism; three members at one new joint make it redundant.

items.prompt: A sailor must hold a 2000 N load using a rope around a fixed post, pulling only 50 N by hand. The rope-post friction coefficient is 0.25. Using T_load/T_hand = e^(μβ) with no safety factor, which of the listed wraps is the smallest that holds the load?

options.label: 3.5 turns
2.0 turns
1.5 turns
2.5 turns

rubric: Need e^(0.25β) ≥ 40, so β ≥ 14.8 rad ≈ 2.35 turns; 2.5 turns is the smallest listed wrap that suffices.
1.5 and 2.0 turns give ratios of about 10.5 and 23; 3.5 turns works but is not the minimum.
